items.task: Recall the requirements to qualify as an IRC Section 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization.
items.stem: Which organization is most likely to qualify for federal income tax exemption as a charitable organization?
options: A nonprofit organized and operated only to provide free legal services to low-income people
An association of local car dealers organized to promote the interests of the automobile industry and of its dealer members
A social club providing recreation to its members, funded by member dues and food and drink sales at the clubhouse
A corporation organized to support and endorse candidates for public office in local, state, and national elections
items.rule_line: A 501(c)(3) organization must be organized and operated exclusively for exempt purposes, with no private inurement and no political campaign activity.

why.A: A charitable organization must be organized and operated exclusively for exempt purposes, and no net earnings may benefit private individuals.
why.B: A business league promotes the common business interests of members and is exempt under a different provision.
why.C: A social club serves its members' personal enjoyment and is exempt under a different provision.
why.D: Participating in a political campaign is not permitted for a charitable organization.

items.blueprint_tag: TCP Area II / Group E / 501(c)(3) requirements / Remembering & Understanding

items.task: Recall the events that would cause an entity to lose its tax-exempt status.
items.stem: A public charity has operated a food bank for many years. Which event would most likely cause it to lose its tax-exempt status?
options: The charity pays its executive director a reasonable salary for her full-time services to the food bank each year
The charity's board pays itself a large share of the net income each year instead of using it for the food bank
The charity earns 15% of its gross income from an unrelated trade or business that is not substantial
The charity spends a small part of its activities on lobbying for legislation related to hunger
items.rule_line: A charity loses exemption if it engages in private inurement, substantial non-exempt activity, or political campaign activity.

why.A: Reasonable compensation for services is not private inurement.
why.B: Private inurement, where net earnings benefit insiders, is prohibited and can result in revocation of exemption.
why.C: An insubstantial unrelated business does not cost exemption; the income is subject to unrelated business income tax.
why.D: An insubstantial amount of lobbying is permitted for a charity.

items.blueprint_tag: TCP Area II / Group E / Loss of tax-exempt status / Application

items.task: Recall the different types of unrelated business income for tax-exempt organizations for tax purposes.
items.stem: Which activity of a tax-exempt organization is most likely to produce unrelated business income?
options: A charity selling donated clothing in a thrift shop that is staffed entirely by unpaid volunteers of the charity
A museum selling catalogs and reproductions of the works in its own permanent collection in its gift shop
A university regularly operating a commercial bakery that sells to the general public
An educational charity receiving dividends and interest from its investment portfolio of stocks and bonds
items.rule_line: Unrelated business income comes from a regularly carried on trade or business not substantially related to the exempt purpose, subject to exclusions.

why.A: Sales of donated merchandise by volunteers are excluded from unrelated business income.
why.B: Sales of items closely related to the museum's exempt purpose are related business income.
why.C: A regularly carried on trade or business that is not substantially related to the exempt purpose produces unrelated business income.
why.D: Dividends, interest, and similar passive income are excluded from unrelated business income.

items.blueprint_tag: TCP Area II / Group E / UBI types / Remembering & Understanding

items.task: Recall the different types of unrelated business income for tax-exempt organizations for tax purposes.
items.stem: Riverstone Foundation, a tax-exempt organization, owns a building it leases to a for-profit tenant for purposes unrelated to its exempt activities. It bought the building for $1,000,000, financed in part with a loan. For 2026 the average acquisition indebtedness is $400,000 and the average adjusted basis is $1,000,000. Rent is $150,000 and directly related expenses, including depreciation, are $50,000. It has no other unrelated business activity and takes the $1,000 specific deduction. What is its unrelated business taxable income?
items.rule_line: Income from debt-financed property is unrelated business income in proportion to average acquisition indebtedness over average adjusted basis.

why.A: The debt-financed percentage is $400,000/$1,000,000 = 40%. Net rent is $150,000 - $50,000 = $100,000, of which 40% ($40,000) is unrelated debt-financed income. Less the $1,000 specific deduction: $39,000.
why.B: Omits the $1,000 specific deduction.
why.C: Includes all of the net rent instead of the debt-financed percentage.
why.D: Includes all of the net rent and omits both the debt-financed percentage and the specific deduction.

items.blueprint_tag: TCP Area II / Group E / UBI types / Application
